blocks.text: ESAB India is the Indian listed arm of ESAB Corporation (Delaware, USA), which holds 73.72% through ESAB Holdings Ltd, UK (37.31%) and Exelvia Group India BV, Netherlands (36.41%) [F] (AR2026 p.22) [F] (AR2026 p.41). It makes and sells welding and cutting products: welding consumables (electrodes, flux-cored and solid wires, SAW flux), arc welding and cutting equipment, and gas-control equipment, and it trades group-made products in India [F] (AR2026 p.49) [F] (AR2026 p.141). FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 1,508.15 crore, up 9.80% [F] (AR2026 p.108) [MC] (AR2026 p.21).

The company earns money in three ways [F] (AR2026 p.141). (1) Manufactured goods: Rs 1,052.70 crore, 69.8% of revenue [E]. (2) Traded goods: Rs 321.21 crore, 21.3% [E]. (3) Engineering, support and consulting services: Rs 124.59 crore, plus Rs 3.50 crore of management services. Together these are 8.5% of revenue [E]. **Essentially all service revenue is billed to ESAB group entities**: related-party service income was Rs 124.63 crore against Rs 124.59 crore of reported engineering services [F] (AR2026 p.157) [AI].

items: End markets: the company lists automotive, general fabrication and construction, pipelines and pipemills, power, process industry, railways, shipbuilding and offshore, transport and mobile machinery, and repair and maintenance for steel, cement, power and mining [F] (AR2026 p.39). **No percentage split by end market is disclosed** [F] (AR2026 p.165).

Product split: the BRSR classifies turnover by NIC code as 71% 'Fabrication Technology' under NIC 2592 and 29% under NIC 2710 [F] (AR2026 p.39). Our reading is that this approximates consumables versus equipment, but the company does not label it that way [AI].
Geography: India Rs 1,249.51 crore (83.2%) and outside India Rs 252.49 crore (16.8%) of contract revenue in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.166) [E]. The BRSR puts exports at 'about 17%' [F] (AR2026 p.39).

Customer profile: 69% of sales go through 393 dealers and distributors. The top 10 dealers account for 26% of dealer sales [F] (AR2026 p.47). No single customer exceeds 10% of sales [F] (AR2026 p.142). Related parties took 22.4% of revenue from operations in FY26 [E] (AR2026 p.157).
Structure: there are no subsidiaries, JVs or associates [F] (AR2026 p.22). The company runs three plants: Ambattur and Irungattukottai in Tamil Nadu, and Kalmeshwar in Nagpur [F] (AR2026 p.88).

blocks.text: Data-integrity warning. Our statements data feed returned only Dec-2005 to Dec-2007 annual figures, with sales of Rs 235-339 crore, and no quarterly data [F] (NUMBERS). Every DCF value, trading multiple and rule-based flag in the feed is computed on that 2007 base, while price (Rs 5,394) and market cap (Rs 8,304 crore) are current [F] (NUMBERS). The model's base-year sales of Rs 339 crore is about 22.5% of FY26 revenue [E]. We report the model outputs because they are the only permitted valuation source, but **we treat them as not decision-useful** (see the valuation sections). Operating analysis in this report rests on the FY26 annual report.

This is not a recent listing. The company was incorporated on 10 November 1987, began operations in July 1988 and is listed on BSE (500133) and NSE (ESABINDIA) [F] (AR2026 p.111) [F] (AR2026 p.86). The evidence base is thin in a different way. We have one annual report (FY26), a CARE rating withdrawal note from July 2020, a short exchange-announcement list and a screener profile [F] (RATING) [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS). **No earnings-call transcripts, investor presentations or quarterly financials were available.** The company states it does not meet institutional investors or analysts, and that only the Chairman is authorised to do so and did not in the past 12 months [F] (AR2026 p.86). Q1 FY27 results were approved on 11 August 2026, but the figures are not in our evidence set [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS).

blocks.text: Driver classification [AI]: #1, #2, #5 and #6 are structural (franchise and capital-light model). #3 and #4 are company-specific, and they depend on how the parent allocates work and export orders. #7 is cyclical.

items: 1. **Arm's-length growth is mid-single-digit.** Stripping out related-party revenue, third-party revenue grew about 6.4% in FY26 (Rs 1,100.1 crore to Rs 1,170.2 crore), against 23.6% growth in related-party revenue [E] (AR2026 p.141, p.157). The 9.8% headline depends on the parent [AI].

2. **Exports are effectively intra-group.** Related-party sales and services to overseas group entities were about Rs 250.5 crore, roughly 99% of the Rs 252.49 crore 'outside India' revenue [E] (AR2026 p.157, p.166). The export story is a group transfer-pricing story, not a market-share win [AI].

3. **A brand the company does not own.** The trademark licence fee to ESAB Europe GmbH was Rs 51.93 crore, 3.44% of revenue, in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.144) [E]. That is about 19% of EBITDA [E]. The rate and duration of the licence are not disclosed [F] (AR2026 p.37).

4. **Margins are flat.** EBITDA margin was 17.9% in FY26 versus 17.8% in FY25 [E] (AR2026 p.108). Employee costs rose to 9.6% of revenue from 8.8% [E]. Management describes 'continued surge in commodity prices', higher energy costs and a weaker rupee [MC] (AR2026 p.20).

5. **Reported PAT growth of 17.8% flatters.** It includes a Rs 30.91 crore gain on the Khardah land sale, net of a Rs 13.65 crore labour-code charge [F] (AR2026 p.146). Excluding the net exceptional, PAT grew about 10.5% [E].

6. **Related-party receivable quality.** EWAC Alloys (a group entity in India) owed Rs 48.85 crore against about Rs 87.1 crore of annual billings, which is about 205 days [E] (AR2026 p.157, p.160). This compares with about 49 days for third-party receivables [E].

7. **Domestic demand is weak and management will not forecast.** Management says 'The short-term outlook remains challenging' and the medium term has 'multiple external dependencies' [MC] (AR2026 p.21). Overall fabrication growth was 'low' [MC] (AR2026 p.21).

8. **Inventory provisioning is rising.** The provision for excess and obsolete inventory went from Rs 8.88 crore to Rs 15.53 crore (+75%) and is a key audit matter [F] (AR2026 p.131) [F] (AR2026 p.97).

9. **Compliance slippage.** Import payables of Rs 3.82 crore were outstanding beyond FEMA timelines [F] (AR2026 p.140). MSME interest is accrued and unpaid (Rs 3.51 crore cumulative) [F] (AR2026 p.140). The auditor modified its books-of-account reporting because payroll backup is held outside India [F] (AR2026 p.99) [F] (AR2026 p.168). CIT(A) upheld income tax penalties of Rs 1.23 crore and Rs 21.87 lakh on 20 August 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS).

10. **Valuation cannot be underwritten from our model.** The only permitted valuation inputs are built on 2007 data [F] (NUMBERS). There is no defensible fair-value anchor in this report, and the price sits 26.4% below its 52-week high [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: The consensus framing of ESAB India, as reflected in our own earlier board notes, is a consumables-and-distribution franchise with near-zero capital intensity [AI] (BOARD). The FY26 annual report supports the capital-light, high-ROCE part [F] (AR2026 p.165). It complicates the growth part. **Roughly a fifth of revenue and nearly all export and service growth now depend on transactions with the parent group, at prices the parent sets.** A further 3.44% of revenue flows back to the parent as a trademark fee [E] (AR2026 p.144, p.157). Arm's-length domestic growth was about 6.6% [E]. Our variant view [AI] is that the stock behaves less like an independent Indian industrial compounder and more like a captive subsidiary whose minority economics depend on group transfer-pricing policy. That cuts both ways. The parent can keep feeding GCC and export volume. It can also re-price royalties or move work elsewhere, and none of these terms are disclosed.

blocks.text: The franchise is old. It was assembled between 1987 and 1994 by acquiring the welding businesses of Philips/Peico, Indian Oxygen and Flotech, and merging Maharashtra Weldaids [F] (RATING). What is recent is the business mix. The group engineering, GCC and R&D services line now makes up 8.5% of revenue [E] (AR2026 p.141). The parent changed in 2022 when ESAB separated from Colfax [F] (AR2026 p.155), and our screener profile still names Colfax as ultimate owner [F] (SCREENER), so that source is stale. Two of three independent directors joined in 2025 and the Chairman changed in May 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.18). The board's institutional memory is therefore concentrated in the MD (on the board since 2013) and the CFO (CFO since 2005) [AI].

blocks.text: Gross margin proxy (revenue less materials and traded goods) was 41.7% in FY26 [E] (AR2026 p.108). The EBITDA margin was much lower at 17.9% [E]. Our read [AI] is that value is captured at the consumable formulation and brand level, not in metal conversion. Part of the brand rent is paid away to the parent. Traded goods grew only 0.2% [E], which suggests the company's own manufacturing is where growth came from in FY26.

Net fixed assets (PPE + ROU + CWIP + intangibles) were Rs 153.58 crore against revenue of Rs 1,508 crore, so revenue is about 9.8x net fixed assets [E] (AR2026 p.107). blocks.text: Without revenue by product, we can only frame this qualitatively [AI]. General-purpose electrodes and solid wires sold through dealers are the most commodity-like lines. Dealers decide the brand at the counter, and local producers compete on price [AI] (BOARD). Flux-cored, specialty alloy and code-qualified consumables are differentiated by procedure qualification. Equipment is differentiated by brand and service. The company does not disclose the mix of specialty versus general consumables, so the share of revenue protected by qualification is unknown [F] (AR2026 p.165).

The company reports a single operating segment, 'fabrication technology', under Ind AS 108. The CODM reviews the business as one unit [F] (AR2026 p.165). **Segment margins are not disclosed.** The only splits available are by revenue type and by geography [F] (AR2026 p.141) [F] (AR2026 p.166).

subsections.title: Deep dive 1: group engineering and GCC services

blocks.text: Position in the value chain: ESAB India sells engineering, support, consulting and R&D services to ESAB group companies, using Indian talent cost [MC] (AR2026 p.21). blocks.text: Where evidence was thin: no earnings-call transcripts, no quarterly data, no peer data, no capacity or volume data, no royalty terms, no third-party customer names, and statements data limited to 2005-2007. The rating note is from 2020 and is a withdrawal [F] (RATING). A prospectus is not relevant for this long-listed company and was not available.

summary.one_line: ESAB India is a debt-free, 60%-ROCE welding franchise whose headline 9.8% FY26 growth rests increasingly on parent-group exports and services, while arm's-length growth is about 6% and 3.44% of revenue goes to the parent as royalty; our valuation model runs on 2007-era inputs and cannot anchor a view on price.
bull_points: [F] Capital-light and debt-free: ROCE 60.0%, ROE 52.3%, capex about 2% of revenue and no borrowings (AR2026 p.22, p.165).
[E] Cash-backed earnings: FY25-FY26 cumulative CFO of Rs 379.5 crore against PAT of Rs 382.1 crore (0.99x), funding a 69% payout (AR2026 p.4, p.109).
[E] Group engineering and GCC services grew 36.5% to Rs 124.59 crore, adding about a quarter of FY26 revenue growth on minimal capital (AR2026 p.141).
[E] Five-year compounding: total revenue CAGR about 13.9% and PAT CAGR about 25% over FY22-FY26 (AR2026 p.4).
[F] Clean audit: unmodified opinions from Deloitte, a single conventional KAM on inventory, audit trail operating (AR2026 p.97, p.100).
bear_points: [E] Third-party (non-group) revenue grew only about 6.4% in FY26, against 23.6% for related-party revenue, which is now 22.4% of revenue (AR2026 p.157).
[E] About 99% of 'outside India' revenue (Rs 252.49 crore) goes to ESAB group entities, so exports are an allocation decision by the parent, not market share won (AR2026 p.157, p.166).
[F] Trademark fee to ESAB Europe of Rs 51.93 crore (3.44% of revenue, about 19% of EBITDA) on undisclosed terms; the brand is rented, not owned (AR2026 p.144).
[E] Operating EBITDA margin flat at 17.9%, unhedged, with a 5% input-cost shock worth about -16% of EBITDA; the 17.8% PAT growth includes a net Rs 17.26 crore exceptional gain (AR2026 p.108, p.146).

[F] Valuation unanchored: our statements data and DCF are built on Dec-2007 figures (sales Rs 339 crore against FY26 Rs 1,508 crore), so the model's fair values and the 153.8x P/E are unusable (NUMBERS).
watch_points: Q2 FY27 results on 4 Nov 2026: revenue growth against FY26's 9.8% and operating EBITDA margin against 17.9%; possible interim dividend (ANNOUNCEMENTS).
Commodity and rupee pass-through: management flagged Q4 FY26 pressure from commodities, energy and a weaker rupee (AR2026 p.20).
Next step in the income tax penalty dispute after CIT(A) upheld Rs 1.23 crore and Rs 21.87 lakh on 20 Aug 2026 (ANNOUNCEMENTS).
Related-party receivable from EWAC Alloys (Rs 48.85 crore, about 205 days of billings) and third-party debtor days (about 49) at the next balance sheet (AR2026 p.160).
Correction of the statements data feed and re-run of the DCF on FY26 figures before any valuation conclusion.
guidance: No quantitative revenue, margin, capex or utilisation guidance was given; no earnings-call transcript was available.
